title: How do we guess Karnataka's hidden value?
description: The values of five neighbouring states are averaged to estimate the hidden rice and wheat value of Karnataka. The video gives a range and breaks Keeko's doubt that the average is the exact value.
teaching_notes: One idea: neighbours give a good guide, and an average of them gives an estimate and not an exact value. Watch for students who give the average as the true answer.

source: Use the neighbours' values to guess Karnataka's value: Goa +
video_script.why: The child can read one value on the rice and wheat scale and now guesses a hidden one from its neighbours.
video_script.substitution: Look at the neighbours, average their values, and give a range around the average as an estimate.
video_script.anchor: the book's rice and wheat map, where the value of Karnataka is hidden
video_script.wrong_answer: Karnataka must be exactly fifty nine point six
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko averages the five neighbours and gives the average as the exact value.
video_script.payoff_line: karnataka is probably a rice leaning value of about sixty to eighty

final_answer.value: A rice leaning value of about +60 to +80, an estimate
final_answer.spoken: karnataka is probably a rice leaning value of about sixty to eighty, an estimate

maths_rules: neighbours' values: Goa +57, Kerala +79, Tamil Nadu +85, Andhra Pradesh +92, Maharashtra -15
four of the five neighbours are strongly rice; Maharashtra is slightly towards wheat
Karnataka is probably around this or a little above, so about +60 to +80; this is an estimate
slip: the average of the neighbours is a guide, not the exact value of Karnataka
video_script.design: One idea: guess a hidden value from its neighbours and give a range. The wrong idea is that the average is exact. A map with Karnataka hidden and its five neighbours lit stays on screen all video.
open_questions: The neighbour values come from the worklist; the map figure is not in the extracted book text, so they could not be checked against it.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='map'/>On the rice and wheat map, the value of Karnataka is hidden.
<bookmark mark='nbr'/>Its neighbours are Goa plus fifty seven, Kerala plus seventy nine, and Tamil Nadu plus eighty five.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Andhra Pradesh is plus ninety two, and Maharashtra is minus fifteen.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can we guess the hidden value of Karnataka from the values of its neighbours?

narration: <bookmark mark='near'/>States that lie close together often eat in a similar way.
<bookmark mark='same'/>The neighbours of a state tell us about it.
<bookmark mark='guess'/>From them we can make a guess. A guess like this is called an estimate.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks Karnataka must be exactly fifty nine point six, the average of the neighbours.
<bookmark mark='range'/>But the neighbours are different states, and Karnataka is its own state.
<bookmark mark='est'/>We give a range as a guess, and not one exact number.
